Real-World Algorithm: 2D Euclidean Distance
In game physics, collision detection, robotics, and navigation engines (such as Google Maps and A* pathfinding), computers calculate the exact straight-line distance between two coordinates (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) millions of times per second.

The Mathematical Formula:
distance = ((x2 - x1)**2 + (y2 - y1)**2)**0.5

The Challenge:
The coordinate variables below are locked. In the editable middle area, write the formula to calculate distance.

Head-Scratcher Alert: Translating this formula requires strict attention to brackets () and operator precedence! You must subtract the coordinates before squaring (** 2), add both squares together, and wrap the entire sum in brackets before taking the square root with ** 0.5.
